questions.question:
If the domain of the function \(f(x)=\log _e\left(\frac{2 x+3}{4 x^2+x-3}\right)+\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x-1}{x+2}\right)\) is \((\alpha, \beta]\), then the value of \(5 \beta-4 \alpha\) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2024, 30 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
For \(\log _e\left(\frac{2 x+3}{4 x^2+x-3}\right)\)

we need \(\frac{2 x+3}{4 x^2+x-3}>0\) and \(4 x^2+x-3 \neq 0\)

\(4 x^2+x-3=4(x+1)\left(x-\frac{3}{4}\right)\)

so \(\frac{2 x+3}{(x+1)\left(x-\frac{3}{4}\right)}>0\)

\(\Rightarrow x \in\left(-\frac{3}{2},-1\right) \cup\left(\frac{3}{4}, \infty\right)\)

For \(\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x-1}{x+2}\right)\)

we need \(-1 \leq \frac{2 x-1}{x+2} \leq 1\) and \(x \neq-2\)

\(\frac{2 x-1}{x+2} \leq 1 \Rightarrow \frac{x-3}{x+2} \leq 0 \Rightarrow-2<x \leq 3\)

\(\frac{2 x-1}{x+2} \geq-1 \Rightarrow \frac{3 x+1}{x+2} \geq 0 \Rightarrow x<-2\) or \(x \geq-\frac{1}{3}\)

So \(\cos ^{-1}\) part gives \(x \in\left[-\frac{1}{3}, 3\right]\)

Overall domain \(=\left[-\frac{1}{3}, 3\right] \cap\left[\left(-\frac{3}{2},-1\right) \cup\left(\frac{3}{4}, \infty\right)\right]=\left(\frac{3}{4}, 3\right]\)

Thus \(\alpha=\frac{3}{4}, \beta=3 \Rightarrow 5 \beta-4 \alpha=15-3=12\)

The second equation is

\(z^3+2z^2+2z+1=0\).

It factors as

\((z+1)(z^2+z+1)=0\).

Thus its roots are

\(z=-1\)

and the two roots satisfying

\(z^2+z+1=0\), for which \(z^3=1\) and \(z\ne1\).

For \(z=-1\), the first polynomial gives

\(1985\equiv2\pmod3\)

and

Therefore,

Both roots of \(z^2+z+1=0\) are common roots.

Hence, the number of common roots is \(2\), which is option D.

Since \(f(x)\) is differentiable on \(\mathbb{R}\), it must be continuous at \(x=1\).

Continuity at \(x=1\) gives \(1^2+3(1)+a=b(1)+2\).

So \(4+a=b+2\)... \((1)\)

Now left derivative at \(x=1\) is \(\left.\frac{d}{dx}(x^2+3x+a)\right|_{x=1}=2(1)+3=5\).

Right derivative at \(x=1\) is \(\left.\frac{d}{dx}(bx+2)\right|_{x=1}=b\).

For differentiability at \(x=1\), \(b=5\).

Using \(4+a=b+2\), we get \(4+a=5+2\).

So \(a=3\).

Therefore \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2+3x+3,&x\leq1\\5x+2,&x>1\end{cases}\).

Now \(\int_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,dx=\int_{-2}^{1}(x^2+3x+3)\,dx+\int_{1}^{2}(5x+2)\,dx\).

\(\int_{-2}^{1}(x^2+3x+3)\,dx=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}+\frac{3x^2}{2}+3x\right]_{-2}^{1}\).

At \(x=1\), \(\frac{x^3}{3}+\frac{3x^2}{2}+3x=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{3}{2}+3=\frac{29}{6}\).

At \(x=-2\), \(\frac{x^3}{3}+\frac{3x^2}{2}+3x=-\frac{8}{3}+6-6=-\frac{8}{3}\).

So \(\int_{-2}^{1}(x^2+3x+3)\,dx=\frac{29}{6}-\left(-\frac{8}{3}\right)=\frac{45}{6}=\frac{15}{2}\).

Also \(\int_{1}^{2}(5x+2)\,dx=\left[\frac{5x^2}{2}+2x\right]_{1}^{2}\).

So \(\int_{1}^{2}(5x+2)\,dx=\left(10+4\right)-\left(\frac{5}{2}+2\right)=14-\frac{9}{2}=\frac{19}{2}\).

Therefore \(\int_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,dx=\frac{15}{2}+\frac{19}{2}=17\).

questions.explanation:
Let the numbers selected from sections \(A,B,C\) be \(a,b,c\), respectively.

We need \(a+b+c=15\), with \(a,b,c\geq4\), \(a\leq8\), and \(b,c\leq6\).

The possible triples are \((7,4,4),(6,5,4),(6,4,5),(5,6,4),(5,5,5),(5,4,6),(4,6,5),(4,5,6)\).

For \((7,4,4)\), the number of selections is \({}^8C_7{}^6C_4{}^6C_4=8\times15\times15=1800\).

For \((6,5,4)\) and \((6,4,5)\), the combined number is \(2\times{}^8C_6{}^6C_5{}^6C_4=2\times28\times6\times15=5040\).

For \((5,6,4)\) and \((5,4,6)\), the combined number is \(2\times{}^8C_5{}^6C_6{}^6C_4=2\times56\times1\times15=1680\).

For \((5,5,5)\), the number is \({}^8C_5({}^6C_5)^2=56\times6\times6=2016\).

For \((4,6,5)\) and \((4,5,6)\), the combined number is \(2\times{}^8C_4{}^6C_6{}^6C_5=2\times70\times1\times6=840\).

Therefore, the total number of selections is \(1800+5040+1680+2016+840=11376\).

questions.question:
Let \(\alpha=\sum_{k=0}^n\left(\frac{\left({ }^n C_k\right)^2}{k+1}\right)\) and \(\beta=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\left(\frac{{ }^n C_k{ }^n C_{k+1}}{k+2}\right)\). If \(5 \alpha=6 \beta\), then \(n\) equals ........... .

 

[JEE Main 2024, 30 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Using \(\dfrac{{}^{n}C_k}{k+1}=\dfrac{{}^{n+1}C_{k+1}}{n+1}\),

we get \(\alpha=\dfrac{1}{n+1}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{n}{}^{n}C_k{}^{n+1}C_{k+1}\).

Since \({}^{n+1}C_{k+1}={}^{n+1}C_{n-k}\),

Vandermonde's identity gives \(\alpha=\dfrac{1}{n+1}{}^{2n+1}C_n\).

Also, \(\dfrac{{}^{n}C_{k+1}}{k+2}=\dfrac{{}^{n+1}C_{k+2}}{n+1}\).

Therefore, \(\beta=\dfrac{1}{n+1}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}{}^{n}C_k{}^{n+1}C_{k+2}\).

Since \({}^{n+1}C_{k+2}={}^{n+1}C_{n-k-1}\),

Vandermonde's identity gives \(\beta=\dfrac{1}{n+1}{}^{2n+1}C_{n-1}\).

Hence \(\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha}=\dfrac{{}^{2n+1}C_{n-1}}{{}^{2n+1}C_n}=\dfrac{n}{n+2}\)

Given \(5\alpha=6\beta\),

we have \(\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha}=\dfrac{5}{6}\)

Therefore, \(\dfrac{n}{n+2}=\dfrac{5}{6}\)

This gives \(6n=5n+10\),

so \(n=10\)

[JEE Main 2024, 30 Jan (Shift 2)]

The area of the region enclosed by the parabola \((y-2)^2=x-1\), the line \(x-2 y+4\) \(=0\) and the positive coordinate axes is ......... .

 

[JEE Main 2024, 30 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The parabola \((y-2)^2=x-1\) can be written as \(x=(y-2)^2+1=y^2-4y+5\).

The line \(x-2y+4=0\) can be written as \(x=2y-4\).

The line meets the positive \(y\)-axis when \(x=0\), giving \(y=2\).

The parabola meets the positive \(x\)-axis when \(y=0\), giving \(x=5\).

The line and the parabola meet when \(y^2-4y+5=2y-4\).

Thus \(y^2-6y+9=0\).

Therefore, \((y-3)^2=0\), so the point of contact is \((2,3)\).

For \(0\leq y\leq2\), the region lies between the \(y\)-axis and the parabola.

For \(2\leq y\leq3\), the region lies between the line and the parabola.

Hence \(A=\displaystyle\int_0^2(y^2-4y+5)dy+\int_2^3\left[(y^2-4y+5)-(2y-4)\right]dy\).

The first integral is \(\left[\dfrac{y^3}{3}-2y^2+5y\right]_0^2=\dfrac{8}{3}-8+10=\dfrac{14}{3}\).

The second integrand is \(y^2-6y+9=(y-3)^2\).

Therefore, the second integral is \(\left[\dfrac{(y-3)^3}{3}\right]_2^3=0-\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)=\dfrac{1}{3}\).

Thus \(A=\dfrac{14}{3}+\dfrac{1}{3}=5\).

questions.question:
Let \(Y=Y(X)\) be a curve lying in the first quadrant such that the area enclosed by the line \(Y-y=Y^{\prime}(x)(X-x)\) and the co-ordinate axes, where \((x, y)\) is any point on the curve, is always \(\frac{-y^2}{2 Y^{\prime}(x)}+1, Y^{\prime}(x) \neq 0\). If \(Y(1)=1\), then \(12 Y(2)\) equals ......... .

 

[JEE Main 2024, 30 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
At the point \((x,y)\), the tangent is

\(Y-y=Y'(x)(X-x)\)

Its intercept on the \(X\)-axis is

\(X=x-\dfrac{y}{Y'(x)}\)

Its intercept on the \(Y\)-axis is

\(Y=y-xY'(x)\)

The area enclosed by the tangent and the coordinate axes is

\(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x-\dfrac{y}{Y'(x)}\right)\left(y-xY'(x)\right)\)

As \(y-xY'(x)=-Y'(x)\left(x-\dfrac{y}{Y'(x)}\right)\), the area is

\(-\dfrac{Y'(x)}{2}\left(x-\dfrac{y}{Y'(x)}\right)^2\)

The given condition gives

\(-\dfrac{Y'}{2}\left(x-\dfrac{y}{Y'}\right)^2=-\dfrac{y^2}{2Y'}+1\)

Expanding the left-hand side, we get

\(-\dfrac{x^2Y'}{2}+xy-\dfrac{y^2}{2Y'}=-\dfrac{y^2}{2Y'}+1\)

\(\Rightarrow -x^2Y'+2xy=2\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{2}{x}y=-\dfrac{2}{x^2}\)

The integrating factor is

\(\mathrm{I.F.}=e^{\int-\frac{2}{x}\,dx}=\dfrac{1}{x^2}\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{y}{x^2}\right)=-\dfrac{2}{x^4}\)

Integrating, we get

\(\dfrac{y}{x^2}=\dfrac{2}{3x^3}+C\)

\(\Rightarrow y=\dfrac{2}{3x}+Cx^2\)

Using \(Y(1)=1\), we get

\(\Rightarrow C=\dfrac{1}{3}\)

\(\Rightarrow Y'(x)=-\dfrac{2}{3x^2}+\dfrac{2x}{3}\)

\(\Rightarrow Y'(2)=-\dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac{4}{3}=\dfrac{7}{6}\)

\(\Rightarrow 12Y'(2)=14\)

Consider two circles \(C_1: x^2+y^2=25\) and \(C_2:(x-\alpha)^2+y^2=16\), where \(\alpha \in(5,9)\).Let the angle between the two radii (one to each circle) drawn from one of the intersection points of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) be \(\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{63}}{8}\right)\). If the length of common chord of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) is \(\beta\), then the value of \((\alpha \beta)^2\) equals .......... .

 

[JEE Main 2024, 30 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The radii of the two circles are \(5\) and \(4\), and the distance between their centres is \(\alpha\).

Let \(P\) be one point of intersection and let the angle between the radii at \(P\) be \(\theta\).

\(\sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{63}}{8}\)

The area of the triangle formed by the two centres and \(P\) is

\(\Delta=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 5\times 4\times \sin\theta=10\sin\theta\)

Let \(h\) be the perpendicular distance of \(P\) from the line joining the centres.

\(\Delta=\dfrac{1}{2}\alpha h\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2}\alpha h=10\sin\theta\)

\(\Rightarrow h=\dfrac{20\sin\theta}{\alpha}\)

The line joining the centres bisects the common chord, so its length is

\(\beta=2h=\dfrac{40\sin\theta}{\alpha}\)

\(\Rightarrow \alpha\beta=40\sin\theta\)

\(\Rightarrow (\alpha\beta)^2=1600\sin^2\theta\)

\(\Rightarrow (\alpha\beta)^2=1600\times \dfrac{63}{64}\)

\(\Rightarrow (\alpha\beta)^2=25\times 63=1575\)

Let a line passing through the point \((-1,2,3)\) intersect the lines \(L_1: \frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y-2}{2}=\frac{z+1}{-2}\) at \(M(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)\) and \(L_2: \frac{x+2}{-3}=\frac{y-2}{-2}=\frac{z-1}{4}\) at \(N(a, b, c)\). Then, the value of \(\frac{(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2}{(a+b+c)^2}\) equals ......... .

 

[JEE Main 2024, 30 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(M=(1+3t,2+2t,-1-2t)\) and \(N=(-2-3s,2-2s,1+4s)\).

The points \(M,(-1,2,3)\) and \(N\) are collinear.

Let \(\overrightarrow{PM}=k\overrightarrow{PN}\), where \(P=(-1,2,3)\).

\(\overrightarrow{PM}=(2+3t,2t,-4-2t)\)

\(\overrightarrow{PN}=(-1-3s,-2s,-2+4s)\)

Equating the coordinates,

\(2+3t=k(-1-3s)\)

\(2t=-2ks\)

\(-4-2t=k(-2+4s)\)

From \(2t=-2ks\),

\(t=-ks\)

Substituting \(t=-ks\) in the first equation,

\(2-3ks=-k-3ks\)

\(\Rightarrow k=-2\)

\(\Rightarrow t=2s\)

Substituting \(k=-2\) and \(t=2s\) in the third equation,

\(-4-4s=4-8s\)

\(\Rightarrow s=2\)

\(\Rightarrow t=4\)

\(\Rightarrow M=(13,10,-9)\)

\(\Rightarrow N=(-8,-2,9)\)

\(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=13+10-9=14\)

\(a+b+c=-8-2+9=-1\)

\(\dfrac{(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2}{(a+b+c)^2}=\dfrac{14^2}{(-1)^2}=196\)

The required value is \(196\).
